title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: no goodwill on an overcharged demurrage line
content:
## Scope

Under the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category, commercial goodwill on the demurrage invoice line of a per-container record is never granted on an overcharge. This rule fixes how the line is recomputed for that purpose and the gross figure goodwill can start from. It reads the cargo type of the container's booking.

## Rule

1. Goodwill is never granted on an overcharge: the demurrage line is recomputed from the record's recorded dates, the product on the record and the booking, exactly as the record's final demurrage line is computed, with the slab count of an export record under the combined clock model continuing after the chargeable days of the detention line booked on the record.
2. In that recomputation the rate class comes from the product's equipment class map, except that a reefer-class container counts as reefer class only when its booking has the cargo type reefer, and otherwise counts as dry class.
3. When the booking's cargo type is dangerous goods, every demurrage day rate in the recomputation is raised by the product's dangerous-goods uplift percentage of itself.
4. The recomputed amount is the sum of the day rates, rounded to the cent.
5. The gross goodwill base is the smaller of the amount still open on the line and the recomputed amount.

## Input, judgement, output

> **Input**: the amount still open on the demurrage line, and the recomputed amount of that line.
> **Judgement**: which of the two is smaller?
> **Output**: the smaller figure is the gross goodwill base; any part of the open amount above the recomputed amount is overcharge and takes no goodwill.

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

| Amount still open | Recomputed amount | Gross goodwill base |
|---|---|---|
| USD 650.00 | USD 600.00 | USD 600.00 |
| USD 650.00 | USD 700.00 | USD 650.00 |
| USD 650.00 | USD 650.00 | USD 650.00 |

## Points of judgement

**Q: Does the recomputation follow what the customer says the gate-out date was?**
A: No. It uses the record's recorded dates, the product on the record and the booking.

**Q: The reefer unit carried general cargo. At which class is it recomputed?**
A: At the dry class, because its booking's cargo type is not reefer.
